01 / Our thesis

The next chapter
of AI is useful work.

Our thesis begins with a shift: from training models to putting intelligence to work. As inference becomes more accessible, new kinds of products and workflows become possible.

Agents connect that capability to productivity. They need efficient compute, reliable infrastructure and real problems to solve. We invest across all three.

THE FOUNDATION

Accessible intelligence.

THE ENABLER

Capable agents.

THE OUTCOME

Measurable productivity.

03 / How we think

Research becomes conviction.

01

Research first.

We go deep into technical shifts and work with researchers to understand what is becoming possible before the market has a name for it.

02

Efficiency matters.

We look for technology that removes a meaningful cost or constraint for the products built on top of it.

03

Technical depth.

We value founders who understand the science, contribute to the tools and can turn a difficult problem into a working product.

04

Real demand.

We ask what work a product completes, who needs it and why they will pay. Customer value is the foundation of our conviction.

06 / Research perspective

THE INFERENCE ECONOMY

From models that answer
to agents that act.

Read our perspectiveClose perspective+

The value of AI becomes tangible when it changes how work gets done. We focus on the systems that connect model capability to that outcome: compute that makes deployment practical, infrastructure that makes agents reliable and applications that solve a customer's problem.

These layers reinforce one another. More efficient inference can support more demanding workflows. Better runtimes and evaluation help teams move from a prototype to a dependable product. Applications reveal which capabilities actually matter in practice.

Our starting question is simple: what useful work does this technology enable? We build conviction by tracing the answer from the underlying research to the people who use it.
